# Ingestion and source coverage

The future collector uses signed GitHub deliveries, bounded hydration and overlapping reconciliation. A webhook is an observation, not proof of complete history. Public Events APIs are unsuitable as the authoritative live ledger.

## Delivery pipeline

- Validate HMAC over raw body and expected content/size, identify installation and allowlisted source, persist delivery transactionally, then acknowledge quickly.
- Durable queue/outbox processes delivery idempotently; fetch authoritative objects as needed. Keep webhook event-time facts even if hydration current state is later.
- Canonicalize actor, object, relation and time, link duplicate observations, attach coverage and scope.
- Apply versioned classification/eligibility policies and receipts; do not modify upstream GitHub metadata.
- Update per-window aggregates and contributor/artifact projections; only publish authorized public fields.
- SSE/event invalidation refreshes clients using resumable sequence IDs; normal cached polling fallback; the user sees last updated and gaps.
- Scheduled overlapping incremental scans reconcile source changes; periodic full count and pagination audits catch missed events.
- Late events, corrections and policy changes rebuild affected periods deterministically without inventing event actors.

## Backfill and reconciliation

- Enumerate installation access + allowlisted public repos by ID. Inventory Projects and fields separately.
- Backfill repository PRs/issues/commits/releases with explicit page exhaustion and source counts. No search-only enumeration, because search coverage/caps are unsuitable.
- For every issue/PR paginate timeline, comments, review records, threads and userContentEdits independently; nested first:100 is not completeness.
- Persist per-resource cursors and transactional watermarks only after successful page ingestion; restarted jobs must resume safely.
- Incremental scans use overlapping updatedAt windows and periodic full sweeps. Timeline-specific events may require parent rescans even if parent updatedAt is unreliable.
- Respect Retry-After/rate reset with jitter, per-installation concurrency/budget, exponential backoff, circuit breaker and dead letter queue; never busy-loop 403/429.
- Distinguish 404 due to access/deletion from absence. Redaction/repository visibility checks run ahead of publishing.
- Compare materialized counts/eligible event samples with raw evidence; GraphQL HTTP 200 can still carry errors/partial data.

## Permissions and installation

### Base app repository read

- Metadata (automatic for App)
- Contents (commits, tree/diff evidence, release metadata)
- Issues (issues, labels, comments, triage, subissue/dependency events)
- Pull requests (PRs, reviews, files and threads)

### Organization read

- Projects, for currently audited Projects 1-5 and all future explicitly onboarded Project IDs

### Optional feature read

**Discussions:** Enable only when organization starts using Discussions.

**Actions:** Workflow metadata/evidence only if approved CI metric context is needed.

**Checks:** Check-run/suite evidence only if needed.

**Commit statuses:** Commit status evidence only if needed.

**Deployments:** Public deployment context only if needed.

### Not required

- repository Administration
- Contents write
- Issues write
- Pull requests write
- Members
- Security events/private vulnerability alerts
- Secrets
- organization webhooks management when own GitHub App webhook suffices

**App level credential:** App JWT for recent delivery inspection/redelivery; installation tokens for repository hydration. Do not expose app private key to frontend.

### Subscription candidates

- installation
- installation_repositories
- repository
- push
- pull_request
- pull_request_review
- pull_request_review_comment
- issues
- issue_comment
- label

- issue_dependencies
- issue_relates_to
- projects_v2
- projects_v2_item
- projects_v2_status_update
- release
- pull_request_review_thread

### Optional subscription candidates

- discussion
- discussion_comment
- check_run
- check_suite
- workflow_run
- deployment
- deployment_status

**Verification gate:** Build a checked permission-to-endpoint-to-event matrix using the actual GitHub App registration and canary events. Documentation event availability and field support vary; no production launch until minimum read permissions can hydrate every claimed metric. If Projects cannot be subscribed via chosen App mode, use a documented supported org-webhook path with explicit owner approval, or disable observed Project attribution; never silently add organization admin permission.

### Taxonomy notes

- Label-definition webhook subscription is documented under Metadata read; this differs from issue label application events. Verify retrieval endpoint permissions separately.
- Milestone-definition webhook subscription is documented under Issues OR Pull requests read. Creation/edit/deletion/state action payloads and timestamps need canary verification.
- Project configuration and issue ordering use reviewed public receipts unless exact actor-bearing events are proven. No new Administration permission is implied.
- Existing governance recognition can accept sanitized repository configuration receipts. Branch-protection webhook collection would require separately reviewed Administration read and is outside baseline scope.

Install only after approved source scope and the permission canary. Use read-only repository access for collection; the public recognition service does not edit upstream issue labels, assignees, Project fields or native relationships. Private source data and credentials never enter public projections.

## Organization history

**Repository identity:** Stable repository ID, with dated owner/name aliases and observed membership intervals.

**Default scope:** Organization contribution windows require evidence that the repository belonged to the organization at event time. Imported prior history can be shown in an explicitly separate inherited-history view.

### Rules

- Repository created_at does not establish when it entered the organization; commit authored_at does not establish when it was integrated here.
- For transferred repositories, record verified transfer/organization-adoption cutoff where available; if unavailable disclose unknown ownership boundary and exclude ambiguous old work from organization-specific comparisons.
- A historical commit imported today remains historical author credit; the act of selecting/migrating it today can separately recognize import stewardship with evidence. Do not present old authored lines as newly written today.
- Default-branch integration time for old commits may be unknown: preserve author/committer dates as those exact facts and avoid inventing an integration timestamp.
- Forks, mirrors, transferred issues, squashed imports and cherry-picks require lineage records and reviewed dedupe decisions. Keep original author provenance when available.
- Changes outside the org do not become organization contributions merely because an account later joins. External PR authors can qualify without membership.
- Never fabricate manual-work volume from API operation count. Administrative batch setup is legitimate stewardship, grouped and labeled in its own category.

**Audit evidence:** source-audit.json and ../docs/SOURCE_AUDIT.md; the source snapshot is time-bounded.

## Receipt contract

### Fields

- id
- category
- contributor_ids
- roles
- artifact_ids
- source_urls
- occurred_at
- submitted_by
- accepted_by
- accepted_at
- acceptance_criteria
- public_summary
- visibility
- status
- supersedes
- dedupe_key
- policy_version

### States

- proposed
- needs_evidence
- accepted
- disputed
- withdrawn
- superseded

### Rules

- Prefer a small reviewed YAML/JSON record in leaderboard repo linked to source PR/issue; no new fields patched into imported v1 contracts.
- Acceptance must verify evidence criteria; bot validation checks structure only.
- Do not create a second research ownership system. Existing issue assignees and review authorities remain source of truth.
- Nominations for external design, mentoring, outreach and sanitized operations work use the same public traceability rules.

Attribution distinguishes author, reviewer, merger, triager, resolver, assignee and automation. A currently assigned person is not automatically the person who performed a past action. Reconciliation can establish a state change without recovering an actor or event time; keep such values unknown and exclude measures that require them.

## Rate budgets and failure handling

**Rest:** Ordinary authenticated/App installation baseline 5000 requests/hour; enterprise/scaling differs. Read response rate headers; the runtime budget is authoritative.

**Graphql:** Ordinary user/App installation baseline 5000 points/hour with separate bucket and scaling; first/last 1..100; max 500000 requested nodes; split deep queries.

**Secondary:** Shared REST/GraphQL concurrency limits exist; use very low bounded concurrency and adaptive pacing, not maximum theoretical throughput. Honor 403/429 and error bodies.

### Sources

- rest_limits
- graphql_limits

Use live headers and API error bodies as runtime authority. Pagination must exhaust each nested connection separately. HTTP success can still contain GraphQL errors; never advance a completeness watermark after a partial page. Replay tests must cover duplicates, out-of-order delivery, gaps, installation removal, renamed or transferred repositories, public-to-private transitions and permission loss.
